title: Unify smart-router evaluation and eliminate redundant regional probes
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem: The smart routing layer currently performs duplicate region/probe work: (1) the policy engine evaluates route eligibility, (2) a separate regional probe pass checks capacity/latency, and (3) the fallback logic consults an outdated fallback table. This has caused N+1 region checks, increasing tail latency and CPU use during high throughput. We also depend on policy-engine v1.9 which lacks a unified evaluation API and forces us to maintain shims.

Goal: Reduce routing evaluation duplication by merging policy evaluation and regional probe results into a single decision path, upgrade to policy-engine v2.1, and deprecate the legacy fallback table. The outcome should be a measurable reduction in p99 latency and CPU, simpler code paths (fewer conditionals), and clearer observability for rollout decisions.

Scope / Acceptance Criteria:
- Integrate policy-engine v2.1 SDK and replace the v1.9 shims in smart-router.
- Implement a single-pass evaluator: policy decisions + region health (latency/capacity) are combined into one scoring operation.
- Remove legacy fallback table references and replace with a configurable fallback policy stored in Config Service.
- Add feature flag (router.unified_eval_v1) to gate behaviour; default off for 2-week canary.
- Add unit + e2e tests covering: policy mismatch, region degradation, graceful fallback, and rollback path.
- Add telemetry: new metrics router.unified_eval.enabled, router.eval.duration_ms, router.eval.score_distribution, and alerts for eval error rate > 0.5%.
- Benchmarks: show >=6% improvement p99 tokens/sec latency and >=12% CPU reduction on staging replay for mixed chat workload.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We intentionally keep the fallback decision config out of the runtime code (Config Service) to enable rapid tuning without deploys. Trade-off: small operational dependency on config rollout; mitigated by validation and schema checks.
- Using policy-engine v2.1 adds a dependency bump and minor API changes. We ran a compatibility layer during early prototyping but decided to migrate directly to v2.1 to avoid long-lived technical debt.
- We will not attempt to merge KV-cache affinity logic in this ticket to keep scope bounded; follow-up ticket will explore cache-aware routing.

Risks / Rollback:
- Risk: policy change bug causing incorrect route scores -> mitigated by canary on 1% of traffic, synthetic traffic tests, and kill-switch feature flag.
- Rollback: flip router.unified_eval_v1 off and redeploy smart-router podset; ensure fallback table remains available for 48 hours in case of rollback.

Notes on testing and metrics capture:
- Use existing replay harness (perf-replay: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-replay/pulls/238) to validate latency/CPU against baseline.
- Collect flamegraphs for top 3 hotspots pre/post for verification. Store artifacts under Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Unified+Router+Perf+Runbook

Deliverables:
- PR merging code: GH-https://github.com/redwood-inference/smart-router/pull/1147
- Migration guide for operators: docs/guides/routing-unified-eval.md
- New Config schema in Config Service: config-id "routing.fallback_policy.v2"
